evidence.exact_quote: MCP tool identity is underscore-only in stored and permission-facing contracts. Slash-form or dual-format `_` / `/` naming canon is retired outside this owner contract; consumer surfaces may display friendly labels but must join back to `{server_slug}_{tool_name}`.
effective state depends on the enabled flag, auth state, server health, project context, and policy/permission state.

items.impact: Implementations can disagree on slug normalization, collision handling, and precedence among enabled, auth, health, context, and policy inputs, producing non-portable permission keys or inconsistent effective states.
items.statement: The owner and underscore-only identity boundaries are explicit, but the source does not define normalization/collision rules for server_slug and tool_name or a deterministic effective-state precedence table with transition oracles.
items.title: Canonical identity and effective-state computation leave deterministic edge cases open

evidence.exact_quote: MCP availability and projected config do not authorize host execution, container exec, Docker socket access, SSH mutation, Kubernetes apply, or cleanup.

items.impact: Builders have a clear fail-closed boundary preventing descriptive MCP host context from becoming execution authority.
items.statement: MI-031 explicitly separates host-capability context projection from host identity and mutation authority, enumerates forbidden execution channels, and preserves degraded and blocked states.
items.title: Containerized host projection has an explicit non-authorizing boundary

evidence.exact_quote: Consumer surfaces may display friendly MCP tool labels, but they must join back to the canonical {server_slug}_{tool_name} identity and must not preserve append-only packet or stale consumer wording beside the live owner sections.

Requested and effective MCP availability remain distinct with requested states authenticated, expired, and not_authenticated and effective states connected, disabled, needs_auth, needs_client_registration, and failed.

items.impact: Localized or duplicate friendly labels may join to the wrong tool, while different consumers may display different requested/effective states for the same inputs.
items.statement: MI-004 through MI-006 pin identity join-back and the two availability vocabularies, but provide neither a stable label-to-tool binding mechanism nor a transition/precedence matrix that can falsify consumer state projections.
items.title: Friendly-label joining and requested/effective transitions are not mechanically specified

evidence.exact_quote: MCP credential binding persists tokens securely, binds stored credentials to the effective remote server URL, invalidates credentials when the configured URL changes, surfaces the four auth lifecycle outcomes, and maps /invalidation plus obl-065 to this owner obligation.

Observability-first MCP bridges for Debug Mode expose read-only APM logs and metrics connectors for production-like failures while keeping that trust model distinct from local probes and without granting mutation authority.

Thread-level MCP surfacing exposes switch, concern trust, and trust state paths in provider/account views so account visibility, persona naming, stage-to-role mapping, and effective provider context remain visible outside Orchestrator pages.

items.impact: In-flight calls may survive URL-bound credential invalidation, and read-only APM or thread trust surfaces may expose sensitive production/account data without defined retention, redaction, access, or audit policy.
items.statement: The owner/consumer and no-mutation boundaries are explicit, but atomic invalidation of concurrent calls and the privacy lifecycle and authorization of APM and provider/account trust disclosures remain untestable.
items.title: Credential revocation and read-only observability still lack lifecycle controls

evidence.exact_quote: MCP schema handling tracks visited $ref values, breaks recursive cycles with {}, logs warnings, enforces maximum depth 32 and 64 KiB size cap, and preserves provider adapter compatibility facts such as Gemini anyOf-to-oneOf rewrites and unsupported const/contentEncoding handling.

MCP OAuth state is keyed by provider, scope, and client semantics; tokens live in the shared credential store, token sharing uses provider+scope, refresh uses compare-and-swap, and PM owns the shared local HTTP listener callback model with explicit bind-address evidence for non-default remote or containerized environments.

items.impact: Provider+scope sharing can cross account, tenant, audience, or client boundaries, while replacing recursive schema branches with an unconstrained object can admit arguments the original schema forbids.
items.statement: MI-013 says OAuth state includes client semantics but token sharing is keyed only by provider+scope, leaving account, tenant, audience, and client isolation unresolved; MI-012's recursive-cycle substitution with {} also lacks a fail-closed exposure rule.
items.title: OAuth token-sharing identity and recursive schema handling create critical boundary ambiguity

evidence.exact_quote: Server-entry config preserves local and remote portable launch shapes, supports OAuth-disabled header-only servers and dynamic client registration, and keeps generated provider adapter config derived and no-secrets by resolving secrets through secret references or auth bindings.

Canonical MCP data records are mcp_server_record, mcp_runtime_availability, and mcp_tool_record with exact fields and enum values for transport_kind, scope, ownership, availability_state, and config_sync_state.

items.impact: Adapters can serialize semantically different local-command shapes or project mutually inconsistent status values, and the debug surface cannot prove which interpretation is canonical.
items.statement: The source contains both command plus args[] and command:string[] portable local-entry descriptions, while MI-016's runtime availability enum is not cross-walked to the earlier connected/disabled effective enum; debug visibility is specified but not the normative reconciliation rule.
items.title: Portable entry shape and canonical status families lack a single reconciliation contract

evidence.exact_quote: MCP resilience uses lazy-load startup, pre-validation before tool dispatch or adapter handoff, cached tool lists as degraded fallback evidence, retries transient failures before eviction, stable OAuth state across reconnects, and refresh triggers from config change, user action, and periodic TTL.

MCP connection pooling is the default for managed server sessions; PM must not use subprocess-per-call for MCP servers except disposable diagnostic probes, and long-lived sessions own lifecycle identity, refresh, health, and teardown state through MCP records.

PM MCP architecture is host-managed at the central registry, health, permissions, and secrets layer, with provider-side adapter state as projection or bridge surface and a three-level lifecycle of Registered in PM, Configured for provider/runtime, and Operational.

items.impact: Concurrent refresh, reconnect, health, dispatch, eviction, and teardown can strand calls, revive stale credentials, or report Operational from stale cache evidence.
items.statement: Lifecycle labels, retries, caching, pooling, and three lifecycle stages are named, but there is no serialized state machine defining concurrent refresh/eviction/teardown ordering, stale-evidence rejection, partial failure, or rollback.
items.title: Managed-session resilience lacks a concurrency-safe lifecycle state machine

evidence.exact_quote: Gemini CLI MCP config and command vocabulary is retired/source-lineage only. PM must not implement Gemini CLI MCP config generation or `gemini mcp add` management as an active provider path; current MCP projection must be proven per active provider/runtime.

items.impact: The explicit negative constraints prevent stale Gemini CLI home and command lineage from being revived as an active provider implementation.
items.statement: MI-021 and MI-022 consistently preserve Gemini CLI MCP facts only as lineage and explicitly forbid active config generation or gemini mcp add setup.
items.title: Retired Gemini CLI MCP behavior is clearly fenced from active implementation

evidence.exact_quote: MCP owner-level flows are exactly auth, list/status, logout, and debug, with auth resolving missing or expired auth, list/status surfacing availability and failures, logout revoking auth binding without deleting server definition, and debug surfacing diagnostics without minting a second status vocabulary.

DirectApi providers use PM-native MCP only, while CLI-provider bridge state is long-lived provider/profile configuration mapped into project-shared or profile-local MCP records; PM may configure, update, repair, or spawn-time regenerate derived provider files only where workspace visibility requires it.

items.impact: Configure, update, repair, install, reconnect, disable, remove, and sync operations can bypass the exact four-flow contract or be inconsistently modeled as sub-actions.
items.statement: The document declares exactly four owner-level flows while nearby provider bridge contracts and GUI contracts require additional lifecycle actions, but no caller-to-flow routing or subordinate command taxonomy reconciles them.
items.title: The exact four-flow contract does not account for provider setup and repair operations

evidence.exact_quote: GUI-facing MCP owner contract reuses auth-state and effective-availability enums for effective tool availability and GUI surfacing, and GUI summary surfaces reference the MCP SSOT instead of re-owning connection-state vocabulary.

The MCP Configuration GUI lists known servers once with user-facing status, remediation, ownership hint, and primary action, while expanded inspectors show runtime availability, auth, tools, logs, sync state, and actions with pending and terminal labels.

items.impact: Remove or Disable may affect the wrong scope without confirmation or rollback, and the row can present a misleading single worst state when enum families disagree or actions remain pending.
items.statement: MI-026 through MI-028 specify labels, rows, inspectors, and actions, but do not define confirmation, scope preview, rollback, stuck-pending recovery, accessibility announcements, localization constraints, or a deterministic crosswalk among the multiple status vocabularies.
items.title: MCP GUI actions and aggregate status remain unsafe and potentially misleading at edge states

evidence.exact_quote: Skill and tool readiness checks evaluate effective MCP lifecycle stage and surface Missing Requirement or degraded readiness in GUI, while first-run provider readiness copy distinguishes credentials, trust, and MCP setup.

Account and profile isolation applies to MCP bridges, keeping provider-native auth_state, workspace_trust, project history, approvals, runtime caches, and OAuth residue profile-local unless a PM-managed overlay explicitly projects a safe shared definition.

items.impact: A shared overlay may leak approvals, trust, history, caches, or OAuth residue across profiles, while first-run copy can report readiness inconsistently when credentials, trust, and MCP setup disagree.
items.statement: MI-029 names readiness disclosures and MI-030 defaults sensitive provider state to profile-local, but neither defines the readiness precedence matrix nor the eligibility, consent, data minimization, revocation, and retention rules for a safe shared overlay.
items.title: First-run readiness and profile overlays lack deterministic privacy-safe rules

evidence.exact_quote: The former MCP_Integration source-preserving bridge is retired after Phase 2B atomized MCP_Integration-S0001 through S0008 into MI-002 through MI-030 and structurally dispositioned S0009, S0010, and S0012. MI-001 remains only as migration lineage for MCP_Integration-S0011 and must not re-own atomized source coverage or use source_preserving_planunit compile mode.

items.impact: The migration-only unit cannot silently regain product ownership or produce implementation work.
items.statement: MI-001 has explicit retirement, ownership, compile-mode, and no-build negative constraints, making its lineage-only role falsifiable.
items.title: MI-001 migration bridge retirement is explicit and bounded

evidence.exact_quote: Imported MCP server from `.claude`/Codex/Warp config defaults ask/disabled until reviewed.
Relative command cwd is project-root only when explicitly resolved and shown.

items.impact: A reviewed import can change before execution, resolve through symlinks outside the project, or overwrite a locally reviewed record during re-import.
items.statement: MI-032 establishes disabled-by-default review and visible cwd resolution, but lacks file identity revalidation at activation, symlink/canonical-path containment, merge/conflict rules, and stale-review invalidation after source hash changes.
items.title: Third-party config import remains vulnerable to stale review and path substitution

evidence.exact_quote: Record versioning increments schema_version on schema hash change and preserves prior schema refs for audit/replay until retention policy expires.

items.impact: Builders cannot determine storage bounds, deletion timing, replay guarantees, or privacy deletion behavior for prior schemas.
items.statement: MI-039 precisely defines resolver order, cache limits, liveness defaults, receipts, and version increments, but delegates prior-schema lifetime to an unnamed retention policy with no owner, duration, deletion oracle, or legal/privacy override.
items.title: Deterministic schema records still depend on an unspecified retention policy

items.statement: MI-033 and MI-036 substantially overlap catalog search, context budgeting, descriptor caching, and result-path parity, but do not nominate a single record owner or enumerate invalidation keys and atomic refresh behavior.
items.title: Lazy catalog and cache PlanUnits overlap without authoritative invalidation semantics

Resolved Authorization header never appears in catalog/debug/log/model context

provider schema subset tests

segments.summary: Reviewed the MCP owner prologue, identity, requested/effective availability, credentials, consumer map, schema/OAuth/config/lifecycle canon, GUI surfacing, MI-002, MI-031, and MI-003. The host-authority fence is strong; identity normalization and effective-state precedence remain under-specified.

Reviewed MI-004 through MI-010, including label join-back, availability disclosure, URL-bound invalidation, consumer ownership, read-only APM trust, and thread account surfacing. Deterministic joins, transition oracles, revocation races, and read-only data governance need stronger contracts.

Reviewed MI-011 through MI-016 across config fields, schema resolution, OAuth listener/token sharing, portable no-secret entries, debug projection, and records/enums. OAuth sharing identity and recursive schema substitution are critical; portable command shape and state crosswalks also conflict or remain absent.

Reviewed MI-017 through MI-022 covering GUI label derivation, cache/retry/eviction, pooled sessions, central registry stages, profile state, and Gemini retirement. Retirement is explicit; refresh, eviction, reconnect, teardown, and stale-evidence races lack a canonical state machine.

Reviewed MI-023 through MI-028 across Cursor evidence, bridge sync, exactly four flows, GUI enum reuse, transport labels, and row/inspector actions. Setup actions are not routed into the exact flow taxonomy, and destructive GUI behavior, accessibility, localization, stuck states, and status aggregation are under-specified.

Reviewed readiness and profile isolation, retired MI-001 migration lineage, migration coverage, third-party config import, and MI-039 schema/liveness defaults. Bridge retirement and resolver defaults are strong; safe overlay, import TOCTOU/path handling, and prior-schema retention remain open.

Reviewed MI-033 through MI-037 covering lazy catalogs, typed JSON fidelity, runtime header hooks, catalog cache, and call liveness. Catalog ownership/invalidation overlaps, null and secret-lifecycle oracles are incomplete, while liveness has useful explicit outcomes completed by MI-039 defaults.
Reviewed MI-038's lazy exposure intent, lineage, constraints, and validation surfaces. Its context-budget and provider-subset acceptance criteria lack measurable workloads and expected outcomes.
